topic_title: Wrong Grignard Product Due to Proton Source

notes_list.title: Check for Acidic Proton
notes_list.basic_overview: Grignard reagents are strong bases as well as nucleophiles and are quenched by compounds containing sufficiently acidic protons.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
OH, NH, SH and COOH groups can consume RMgX before the desired carbonyl addition occurs. Protect or otherwise manage such functional groups when necessary.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Grignard reagents are strong bases as well as nucleophiles and are quenched by compounds containing sufficiently acidic protons. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
